mentions.name: Self-hosted GitHub Actions CI runners
mentions.description: An open-source project that reduces GitHub Actions CI costs by running workflow jobs on self-hosted runners on owned hardware. It aims to fill the gap between local workflow execution tools like act and cloud-based self-hosted runner setups, keeping operations simple, avoiding unneeded features, and treating caching-based efficiency gains as a bonus.
mentions.problem: GitHub Actions CI costs are high, and there is a gap between local workflow execution tools like act and cloud-based self-hosted runner setups for teams that need simple, low-cost ops.
mentions.source_excerpt:
I’m building an open-source project to reduce GitHub Actions CI costs by running jobs on self-hosted runners on owned hardware.
The motivation is to fill the gap between local workflow execution by projects like https://github.com/nektos/act and self-hosted runner setups on the cloud.
